sections.title: Management Summary
sections.content:
Airbus Helicopters is seeking an integration platform that operates entirely within its own data center, supports a move away from legacy Informatica tooling, and enables a broader team (not just a small group of specialists) to build and maintain integrations. The requirements are clear: on-premises execution, enterprise security, proven migration capability, and a path to self-sufficiency. In evaluating responses to this RFP, Airbus Helicopters should weight three criteria that separate platforms which genuinely deliver on this mandate from those that fulfil it on paper only:

1. Genuine ease of use, measured by time-to-first-productive-pipeline for a developer new to the platform, not by feature count.
2. Automated Informatica migration tooling, verified by live demonstration against AH's actual pipeline sample, not by a vendor claim in a slide deck.
3. Embedded AI that operates on-premises, confirmed by a working demonstration in the evaluation environment, not a cloud-only proof of concept.

SnapLogic meets all 114 technical requirements at full compliance. More importantly, it is one of the very few platforms designed from the ground up for exactly this combination: genuine on-premises deployment, a direct migration path from Informatica, and an AI co-pilot embedded in the development environment that no competing on-premises tool can match. SnapLogic was founded by the co-founder of Informatica, and the company understands on-premises enterprise integration at its deepest level. With 15+ years in production, 500+ enterprise customers, and 5 trillion integration records processed monthly, this is a mature platform with a proven track record in regulated industries including aerospace supply chains and defence. Under CEO Brad Stewart and CTO Jeremiah Stone, the platform is now accelerating its AI capabilities, making intelligent automation an integral part of the integration platform rather than a future roadmap item.

The six value drivers below summarise what this means in practice for Airbus Helicopters.

[FEATURE:navy|Lower TCO]Predictable annual subscription with no per-connector surcharges. Forrester confirms 181% ROI over 3 years with under 6-month payback. Automated migration tooling reduces effort by 40–70%.[/FEATURE] [FEATURE:jade|Faster Integration Delivery]Visual drag-and-drop development and AI-generated pipeline creation reduce time from requirement to working integration by 60–80%.[/FEATURE] [FEATURE:blue|Rapid Team Onboarding]Informatica team finds concepts immediately familiar. New developers productive within days. Browser-based IDE with no XML configuration or proprietary scripting.[/FEATURE] [FEATURE:blue|AI Co-Pilot]SnapGPT generates integrations from plain-language descriptions. No other on-premises integration platform offers this.[/FEATURE] [FEATURE:orange|Complete Data Sovereignty]All data processing occurs within AH's own data center on RedHat OpenShift. No operational data ever leaves AH's network.[/FEATURE] [FEATURE:jade|Enterprise Governance]RBAC, SSO with Active Directory, MFA, tamper-proof audit trail, and full version-controlled promotion across Development/Validation/Pre-Production/Production, all included as standard.[/FEATURE]

subsections.title: Platform Reuse - Patterns and Pattern Libraries
subsections.content:
SnapLogic is designed around the principle of reuse. Rather than building each integration from scratch, teams build once and share across the organisation. This is supported at multiple levels of the platform:

- Child pipelines as reusable components: Any pipeline can be called as a child pipeline by other pipelines, passing data in and receiving output. Common patterns (data validation, error handling, canonical transformations, authentication flows) are built once and shared across all consuming integrations.
- Pattern libraries: Integration patterns are catalogued and published within the SnapLogic Org as a shared library. Developers discover and reuse approved patterns rather than re-implementing common logic.
- Parameterised pipeline templates: Pipelines can be designed as templates with configurable parameters, allowing a single integration pattern to serve multiple source systems, target schemas, or business units without duplication.
- RBAC-governed sharing: Shared patterns and templates are published under role-based access control, so the integration centre of excellence at AH can govern which patterns are approved for production use and which are in development.

SnapLogic Platform Overview SnapLogic's platform architecture is designed around a single principle that directly addresses Airbus Helicopters' core requirement: all data processing occurs within AH's own infrastructure. The execution engine, the Ground Plex, runs inside AH's private data center on RedHat OpenShift, the platform already mandated by AH's IT standards. SnapLogic's cloud component handles only pipeline metadata, never operational data, which satisfies both the on-premises mandate and the GDPR and data sovereignty requirements of the RFP. For a team migrating from Informatica, the development model will be immediately familiar, and SnapLogic's SLIM migration tooling accelerates the transition of the existing pipeline estate. The embedded SnapGPT AI assistant accelerates new development without requiring cloud data access, operating solely on pipeline structure and developer prompts.

For a programme of this scale and duration, four vendor evaluation dimensions determine long-term value. Predictable total cost of ownership requires all license tiers, connector module fees, and support costs to be stated transparently as a three-year figure. An independent product roadmap means the platform's strategic direction is controlled by the vendor itself, not subordinated to a parent company's portfolio priorities. Genuine on-premises AI capability means AI-assisted development features operate within the customer's own infrastructure, not as a SaaS-only premium tier. And platform continuity is evidenced by consistent, uninterrupted investment over the past 36 months without strategic repositioning. Each of these dimensions is addressed explicitly in the sections below.

subsections.title: Component: Ground Plex - On-Premises Data Plane
subsections.content:
The Ground Plex is SnapLogic's on-premises execution engine and the core of any Airbus Helicopters deployment. Every pipeline execution, data transformation, and connector call runs inside the Ground Plex, within AH's private data center. Communication with the SnapLogic Manager uses a single outbound HTTPS connection on port 443. No inbound firewall rules are required and no operational data leaves the network boundary.

- Deployed as Docker containers on RedHat OpenShift via SnapLogic-certified Helm charts
- Each node runs multiple JCC (Java Cloud Connector) containers, each capable of 100+ concurrent pipeline executions
- Active-active multi-node configuration: on node failure, workload redistributes automatically across remaining nodes
- Stateless by design: pipeline definitions are stored in the Manager, not on the node, so new nodes are operational within minutes of deployment
- Connector credentials are encrypted and stored locally within the Ground Plex and are never transmitted to SnapLogic infrastructure
- Snaps process data as a continuous stream rather than loading full datasets into memory, giving high throughput with predictable resource consumption

subsections.title: Component: Designer - Visual Pipeline Development IDE
subsections.content:
Figure~\ref{fig:designer-canvas} shows the SnapLogic Designer: pipeline canvas with SnapGPT sidebar, with a pipeline under development.

[IMAGE:assets/images/airbus_rfp/snaplogic-designer-pipeline-canvas.png:SnapLogic Designer: Pipeline Canvas with SnapGPT Sidebar:1.0:designer-canvas]



SnapLogic Designer: pipeline canvas The Designer is SnapLogic's browser-based visual IDE for building integration pipelines, running inside the Manager UI. Pipelines are built by placing Snaps on a canvas and connecting them with data flow links. The visual representation is the executable artefact, with no separate compilation or code generation step. Developers configure Snaps through inline panels, write field mapping expressions using SnapLogic's JavaScript-based expression language, and validate execution against sample data without leaving the IDE.

- Drag-and-drop canvas with left-to-right data flow: Source Snaps → Transform Snaps → Target Snaps
- Snap configuration panels open inline, so developers never need to switch context between design and configuration views
- Expression editor with syntax highlighting, auto-complete, and live schema preview for field mapping
- SnapGPT sidebar is accessible within Designer for AI-assisted pipeline generation, Mapper expression authoring, and error debugging
- AutoSuggest recommends the next most likely Snap based on the current pipeline context, displayed as a watermark on the canvas
- Built-in Validation mode lets developers execute a pipeline against sample data at design time and inspect output at each Snap. Validation data is not persisted and does not leave the Ground Plex.
- Pipeline versioning: Each time a developer creates a version in Designer, SnapLogic stores an immutable snapshot of the pipeline definition. The full version history is browsable, versions can be compared, and a previous version can be restored as a new snapshot, making rollback a deliberate, auditable action. For teams requiring Git-based change control, native Git integration pushes pipeline artefacts (.slpkg packages) to GitLab or GitHub, supporting branch-based development, pull request workflows, and CI/CD-driven promotion across the Development, Validation, Pre-Production, and Production environments.

subsections.title: Component: Snaps & Snap Packs - The Connector Ecosystem
subsections.content:
Figure~\ref{fig:snap-pack-s3} illustrates the breadth of available Snap categories and the 700+ pre-built connectors accessible to all developers.

[IMAGE:assets/images/airbus_rfp/snaplogic-snap-pack-amazon-s3.png:SnapLogic Snap Pack: Amazon S3:1.0:snap-pack-s3]



SnapLogic Snap Pack: Amazon S3 (example) Snaps are the pre-built, configurable building blocks of every SnapLogic pipeline. Each Snap represents a single operation: reading from a database, transforming a field, filtering records, writing to a file, or calling an API. Snaps are grouped into Snap Packs by technology category, such as Oracle, Kafka, HTTP, and SAP. The library covers 700+ Snaps across all major enterprise technologies. Where a pre-built connector does not exist, customers can develop custom Snaps using the SnapLogic Snap SDK (Java).

All Snap execution runs inside the Ground Plex. Connector credentials and data never leave AH's network. Snap Packs are versioned and updated independently of the platform, so connector updates do not require a full platform upgrade. Standard operations are configured declaratively; expressions are used only for custom transformation logic. Snaps are categorised by function: Read (sources), Transform, Write (targets), Parse, Format, Flow control, Error handling, and Script.

subsections.title: Component: Pipeline Execution Modes
subsections.content:
SnapLogic supports three distinct pipeline execution modes, each optimised for different integration patterns. Understanding these modes is important for Airbus Helicopters' integration architecture design.

Table 4 summarises the four execution modes supported by SnapLogic and their relevance to Airbus Helicopters integration scenarios.

[TABLE:simple:Pipeline Execution Modes and AH Relevance::execution-modes]
| Execution Mode | How Triggered | Primary Use Case | AH Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Scheduled Task** | Cron schedule (fixed or dynamic) | Periodic batch extract, daily data loads, recurring reports | Nightly ERP extracts, daily CDC batch windows, periodic file transfers |
| **Triggered Task** | REST API call, file arrival, message queue event | Event-driven integration, on-demand processing, webhook receivers | API-triggered data provisioning, file-arrival processing (SFTP drop), MES event handling |
| **Ultra Task (Ultra Pipeline)** | REST API call with pre-loaded pipeline state | Sub-second latency API responses, real-time data lookups, high-frequency event streaming | Real-time inventory queries, CDC streaming, high-volume message bus processing |
[/TABLE]

subsections.title: Component: SnapGPT - AI Copilot
subsections.content:
SnapGPT is SnapLogic's embedded generative AI assistant, accessible directly within the Designer. No other on-premises-compatible ETL/ELT platform offers a comparable capability for this RFP. SnapGPT operates from the SnapLogic Manager and processes only pipeline metadata and natural language prompts. It has no access to, and never transmits, Airbus Helicopters' operational data.

- Text2Pipeline: A plain-English description of the integration generates a working pipeline with appropriate Snaps, connections, and baseline configuration
- Mapper expression generation: A description of the desired field transformation produces the complete SnapLogic expression
- Auto-documentation: SnapGPT generates human-readable descriptions for every pipeline, Snap, and field mapping without manual input
- AI-assisted debugging: On pipeline failure, SnapGPT analyses the error context and proposes a specific fix
- Describe Pipelines: SnapGPT analyses an existing pipeline and produces a structured description of its logic, connections, and data flow, useful for documentation, handover, and onboarding new team members

See Appendix C for a step-by-step Citizen Integrator user story illustrating how a business analyst at Airbus Helicopters builds a complete integration pipeline using SnapGPT's AI-assisted development capabilities, without requiring coding experience.

subsections.title: On-Premises Deployment: Ground Plex on RedHat OpenShift
subsections.content:
This section covers the on-premises deployment architecture requirements of the RFP, including containerised deployment on OpenShift (P-01, P-04), horizontal and vertical scaling (P-02), high availability (P-03), network port requirements (P-05), and autonomous pipeline deployment via CI/CD (P-06). The Ground Plex is deployed as containerised workloads within Airbus Helicopters' private data center, running on RedHat OpenShift. All pipeline execution, data transformation, and connector activity occurs entirely within AH's network boundary. No customer data is transmitted to or processed by SnapLogic's cloud infrastructure at any point in the integration lifecycle.

The SnapLogic Manager (cloud-hosted) handles only non-data metadata: pipeline definitions stored as JSON, schedules, user accounts, and audit logs. It communicates with the Ground Plex over a single outbound HTTPS connection on port 443, requiring no inbound firewall exceptions on the AH perimeter. The Manager qualifies under the RFP's stated exception for non-data components, subject to formal AH Security approval. SnapLogic supports this process with detailed network architecture documentation, data flow diagrams, and a dedicated security review.

subsections.title: OpenShift Containerised Deployment
subsections.content:
Ground Plex nodes run as Docker containers orchestrated by OpenShift. SnapLogic provides certified Helm charts for deployment. OpenShift's native pod scheduling, resource quotas, and health monitoring apply directly to Ground Plex pods.

- Container deployment: Each Ground Plex node is a JCC (SnapLogic Java Cloud Connector) container. Multiple JCC containers per node can be configured for increased pipeline concurrency.
- Helm charts & configuration: SnapLogic-provided Helm charts parametrise the Ground Plex deployment. Environment-specific configuration (Org name, network settings, resource limits) is managed via values files in the customer's GitLab repository.
- OpenShift SCC note: The Ground Plex startup script requires write access to /etc/snaplogic for key generation. In OpenShift environments with the default restricted-v2 SCC, an anyuid SCC grant or CI/CD build-phase key pre-generation approach must be agreed with AH's OpenShift team prior to deployment. SnapLogic PS will guide this configuration.
- Network proxy support: In environments with a corporate HTTP proxy, Ground Plex JVM arguments must be configured to exclude internal Kubernetes DNS names from proxy routing ( -Dhttp.nonProxyHosts ). SnapLogic documents this configuration explicitly for proxy-enabled OpenShift environments.

subsections.title: Scalability: Horizontal and Vertical
subsections.content:
The Ground Plex architecture is designed for elastic scaling within AH's OpenShift cluster without requiring pipeline re-architecture or downtime.

- Horizontal node scaling: Additional Ground Plex worker nodes are registered to the existing Snaplex (logical group of nodes) and immediately begin receiving pipeline workloads. OpenShift Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) policies can be applied to Ground Plex deployments for demand-driven scaling.
- Vertical scaling: CPU and memory resources per Ground Plex pod are configurable via Helm values. Increasing node resources increases the concurrency and throughput capacity of individual pipeline executions.
- Autonomous pipeline deployment: Pipelines are deployed programmatically via SnapLogic's Migration REST API or the slpkg CLI, enabling full CI/CD pipeline promotion (Development → Validation → Pre-Production → Production) without manual Designer interaction. Each environment is a separately registered Ground Plex with its own resource allocation and RBAC controls.

subsections.title: High Availability Configuration
subsections.content:
Ground Plex supports active-active multi-node HA natively. Multiple Ground Plex nodes registered to the same Snaplex share the execution workload. Node failure causes immediate automatic redistribution of queued and incoming pipeline requests to healthy nodes, with no pipeline interruption for stateless workloads.

- Scheduled pipelines are automatically restarted on available nodes if the executing node fails during execution
- SnapLogic recommends a minimum of 2 Ground Plex nodes for production HA deployments
- Node health is monitored via 20-second heartbeat from Ground Plex to Manager; failed nodes are removed from the active execution pool automatically

subsections.title: Network & Port Documentation
subsections.content: All required network ports are documented in SnapLogic's Groundplex Configuration Guide, provided to AH's network team prior to deployment. The primary connectivity requirement is a single outbound HTTPS/WSS connection (port 443) from each Ground Plex node to SnapLogic's Manager endpoint. No inbound ports are required on the AH network perimeter.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: This deployment model means the integration platform operates entirely within AH's security perimeter, with no operational data leaving the network boundary. It meets the on-premises mandate of the RFP while retaining the management and AI development capabilities of the SnapLogic cloud. The OpenShift-native containerised deployment aligns with AH's existing infrastructure standards, and the no-inbound-firewall architecture eliminates any requirement for network perimeter exceptions.

subsections.title: Connectivity & Connector Ecosystem
subsections.content: This section addresses the connectivity requirements of the RFP, covering database connectors with Change Data Capture (C-01.1 through C-01.7), messaging and event streaming protocols (C-02), file system and storage connectivity (C-03), and aerospace-specific formats including S2000M and STEP/ISO 10303. SnapLogic's connector library covers 700+ pre-built Snaps spanning enterprise applications, relational and NoSQL databases, messaging protocols, file systems, and aerospace-specific data formats. All connectors run within the Ground Plex, so data never leaves AH's network boundary during processing.

subsections.title: Relational Databases & Change Data Capture
subsections.content:
SnapLogic provides native JDBC connectors and built-in CDC capabilities for all major relational databases relevant to Airbus Helicopters' environment. All database connections are established from the Ground Plex to the database server, fully within AH's network.

- Oracle Database v12c+: Native Oracle Snap Pack (JDBC) for read/write/upsert. Full CDC via Oracle LogMiner, captures INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DDL changes in real time. Oracle Exadata is supported via the same Oracle JDBC and CDC stack (Exadata presents a standard Oracle interface to JDBC clients).
- Microsoft SQL Server v2019+: Native SQL Server Snap Pack (JDBC). CDC via SQL Server Change Tracking / Capture, captures all DML changes per-table with LSN-based watermarking.
- PostgreSQL v9.2+: Native PostgreSQL Snap Pack (JDBC). CDC via PostgreSQL logical replication (pgoutput plugin), supports all DML operations with consistent ordering.
- MySQL v5+ / MariaDB v5.5+: Native MySQL/MariaDB Snap Pack (JDBC). CDC via binary log (binlog) replication, captures row-level changes with microsecond timestamps.
- Generic JDBC: Universal JDBC connector for any JDBC-compliant database. Supports DuckDB (in-process analytical DB), SAP HANA, IBM DB2, Teradata, and others via the JDBC driver deployed to the Ground Plex node.
- MongoDB v8+, Neo4j v5.25+, Elasticsearch v8.12+, Splunk Enterprise v7.x+: Native connectors for document, graph, search, and analytics stores.

subsections.title: Messaging & Event Streaming
subsections.content:
SnapLogic supports all major on-premises messaging and event streaming platforms, operating as both producer and consumer within AH's existing message bus infrastructure.

- Apache Kafka v4.0+: Native Kafka Snap Pack. Produces to and consumes from Kafka topics on-premises. Supports key/value serialisation (JSON, Avro, Protobuf), consumer group management, and offset control. Kafka brokers remain entirely within AH's network.
- RabbitMQ: AMQP v0.9.1+, publish to exchanges and consume from queues, both inbound and outbound. Supports durable queues, message TTL, and dead-letter exchange patterns.
- Solace v10.25+: Native SMF (Solace Messaging Format) protocol support via the JMS Snap Pack. Publish to and subscribe from Solace topics and queues. Solace is a common MOM in aerospace manufacturing environments.
- JMS v1.1+: Generic JMS connector for any JMS-compliant broker (IBM MQ, ActiveMQ, Tibco EMS, etc.). Supports both publish/produce (outbound) and subscribe/consume (inbound).
- MQTT v3.1.1 and v5.0: Lightweight publish/subscribe protocol for IoT and sensor data use cases, inbound subscribe and outbound publish.
- AMQP v0.9.1+: Direct AMQP protocol support for publish (outbound) and subscribe (inbound), independent of the RabbitMQ connector.

subsections.title: File Transfer & Storage
subsections.content:
- SFTP: Read and write files from/to SFTP servers. Supports key-based and password authentication. File pattern matching, recursive directory listing, and append mode.
- FTP: Read/write (outbound). Active and passive mode supported.
- SCP: Secure file copy read/write.
- SMB/NFS: Local and network file system read/write. SMB (Windows file shares) and NFS (Unix/Linux) are both supported. Ground Plex mounts shares as local filesystem paths. Enables integration with legacy file-drop integration patterns common in manufacturing environments.
- S3-Compatible Object Storage: Read/write to any S3-compatible on-premises object store (MinIO, Ceph, NetApp StorageGRID, etc.). All S3 API operations (GetObject, PutObject, ListObjects, DeleteObject) supported.
- Google Drive / Google Sheets: Read/write connector for Google Workspace, relevant for AH teams using G Suite for collaboration.

subsections.title: Enterprise Applications
subsections.content:
- SAP HANA: Native SAP HANA connector (JDBC-based). Read from columnar tables, execute stored procedures, and write data to HANA tables.
- Salesforce, ServiceNow, JIRA v1.0+: Native REST API-based connectors. Support CRUD operations, bulk API patterns, and webhook-based inbound event triggers.
- LDAP: Native connector for Active Directory and OpenLDAP. Search, read, and write directory entries. Used for identity resolution and group-based access control workflows.
- Palantir Foundry: Native connector for read/write to Foundry datasets. Relevant for AH's advanced analytics and data platform workloads.
- REST/RESTful APIs: HTTP Client Snap for any REST endpoint, configures HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), headers, authentication (OAuth 2.0, API key, Basic Auth, Bearer), request/response body format (JSON, XML, form-data). Both outbound calls and inbound triggered endpoints (Triggered Tasks) are supported.
- Apache Spark v3.5+: Native connector for distributed processing workloads. Submits Spark jobs and reads results, relevant for large-scale data processing use cases alongside an existing Spark infrastructure.

subsections.title: File Formats & Aerospace-Specific Data
subsections.content:
- Apache Parquet: Native read/write. Columnar format for analytics workloads and data lake integration.
- Apache Iceberg: Read/write via Spark connector and S3-compatible storage integration. Iceberg tables managed by Spark on-premises are accessible as data sources/targets.
- Standard formats: JSON, XML (with XPath/XSLT support), CSV, Excel (.xlsx), Avro, fixed-width, EDI (X12, EDIFACT).
- ASD S2000M (ASD Spec 2000 / iSpec 2200): S2000M is an XML-based standard (SGML subset) used for aircraft parts data exchange, MRO provisioning lists, and inventory management. SnapLogic processes S2000M files via the XML Snap Pack with a custom schema mapping to AH's canonical data model. A fully native S2000M Snap is not available out of the box. SnapLogic PS will scope the schema mapping approach for AH's specific S2000M use cases (provisioning, purchase orders, inventory exchange) during the initial engagement.
- STEP file format (ISO 10303): STEP/AP (Application Protocol) files are the standard exchange format for CAD and PLM product data (used with CATIA, NX, Teamcenter, etc.). SnapLogic handles STEP files as binary/ASCII file transport via SFTP or filesystem Snaps. Native STEP schema parsing (extracting product structure, BOM, geometry metadata) requires either a custom Snap developed against a STEP parser library (Open CASCADE, JSDAI), or integration via a third-party STEP processor using the Script Snap. SnapLogic PS will scope the appropriate approach for AH's PLM integration use cases.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: This connector coverage addresses the full system landscape described in the RFP. The Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB connectors with native Change Data Capture handle AH's core database estate. The Kafka and Solace connectors address the messaging infrastructure. SFTP and SMB connectivity covers supplier and manufacturing file exchange. The S2000M and STEP format requirements for MRO and PLM integration are addressed via the XML Snap Pack and file transport respectively, with mapping approaches scoped by Professional Services for AH's specific use cases.

subsections.title: Pipeline Development, Low-Code Design & SnapGPT AI
subsections.content: This section covers the development capability requirements of the RFP: low-code visual design (D-01), metadata management (D-02), reusable components (D-03), development and validation environment (D-04), auto-documentation (D-05), GitLab integration (D-06), custom development in Java and Python (D-07), SCD Type 2 support (D-08), scheduling (D-09), event triggers (D-10), error handling (D-11), and programmatic API access (D-12). It also covers the citizen development requirements (CD-01 through CD-05), including SnapGPT-enabled self-service pipeline creation and governed approval workflows. SnapLogic's Designer is a browser-based visual IDE for building integration pipelines. Pipelines are built by connecting Snaps on a canvas. The visual representation is the executable artefact, with no separate code generation step. For an Airbus Helicopters integration team with existing Informatica experience, the paradigm will feel familiar: sources, transformations, and targets connected left-to-right, with modular child pipelines as the equivalent of Informatica mapplets.

subsections.title: Visual Low-Code Designer & Ease of Use
subsections.content:
SnapLogic's Designer runs in a standard browser, with no local installation required on the developer's workstation. All pipeline development activity occurs through the Designer UI, which communicates with the SnapLogic Manager over HTTPS. This matters more than it might initially appear: enterprise integration platforms that require local IDE installation, custom Java development environments, or XML-based configuration management impose a hidden per-developer setup and maintenance tax that compounds over the lifetime of the programme. SnapLogic eliminates this entirely. A new team member opens a browser and starts building integrations within the same session. Evaluators should specifically verify how long it takes to make a first productive change to a pipeline on each platform. That single metric often exposes significant differences in practical usability that do not surface in feature checklists.

- Drag-and-drop canvas: Pipelines are built by placing Snaps on a canvas and connecting them with data flow links. Each Snap's configuration panel opens inline, with no context switching required.
- Expression language: SnapLogic's JavaScript-based expression language is used for field mappings, filter conditions, and computed values. Expressions are written inline in Snap configuration fields, with syntax highlighting and auto-complete. The language is intentionally readable by non-developers.
- Mapper Snap: The core transformation component, which maps fields from source schemas to target schemas with expression-based transformation logic. SnapGPT can auto-generate Mapper expressions from natural language descriptions of the desired transformation.
- Conditional flows: The Router Snap branches pipeline execution based on data conditions, equivalent to conditional mappings in Informatica. Multiple downstream branches can be defined with independent processing logic per branch.
- Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 (SCD2): Dedicated SCD Snap implements Type 2 history tracking natively. No custom SQL, stored procedures, or external staging tables required. Tracks effective dates, current/historical record flags, and surrogate key management inline within the pipeline.
- Reusable child pipelines: Pipelines can call other pipelines (child/sub-pipelines), passing data as input and receiving output. This enables modular, reusable integration patterns, equivalent to Informatica mapplets. Child pipelines are versioned and RBAC-controlled independently.
- Catalog of reusable components: Shared pipeline library within the Org. Child pipelines, parameterised templates, and custom Snap Packs are published and discoverable by all authorised developers in the organisation.

subsections.title: Custom Development & Extensibility
subsections.content:
Where standard Snaps do not cover a specific integration requirement, SnapLogic provides multiple extensibility options, all of which execute within the Ground Plex.

- Custom Snaps (Java): Developed using the SnapLogic Snap SDK (Java). Custom Snaps are packaged as JAR files and deployed to the Ground Plex. External Java libraries can be bundled. Custom Snaps appear in the Designer alongside standard Snaps.
- Script Snap (Python / JavaScript): Executes inline Python or JavaScript code within the pipeline. Supports import of external Python libraries (from the Ground Plex's Python environment) and Java libraries via Jython. Configurable Python executable path supports use of specific virtualenv or system Python installations (v2+) on the Ground Plex node.
- Java runtime selection: Ground Plex nodes run on a bundled JVM. Custom Snap Packs can target specific JRE compatibility versions (v7+) via the Snap SDK build configuration, which is relevant for custom Snaps integrating with older Java-based enterprise systems.
- Programmatic pipeline design via REST API: SnapLogic's full REST API supports pipeline creation, modification, cloning, execution, and metadata retrieval. Enables infrastructure-as-code workflows and integration with AH's existing toolchain (Ansible, Terraform, GitLab CI).

subsections.title: Scheduling, Triggers & Execution Modes
subsections.content:
- Fixed & dynamic scheduling: Cron-based schedule triggers for time-driven pipeline execution. Dynamic schedules can be parameterised at runtime via API.
- External event triggers: Triggered Tasks expose pipeline executions as REST API endpoints, callable from any system (orchestrators, portals, other pipelines). File-arrival triggers detect new files on SFTP/filesystem and trigger pipelines automatically. Message queue event triggers fire on new messages in Kafka, JMS, or AMQP queues.
- Ultra Pipelines: High-performance streaming execution mode for high-volume, low-latency data movement (bulk extract, CDC streaming, real-time event processing). Ultra Pipelines sustain billions of records per day at enterprise scale.

subsections.title: Integrated Validation Environment
subsections.content: SnapLogic's built-in Validation mode allows developers to execute pipelines at design time and inspect the data output at every Snap before promotion to test or production. Validation runs entirely within the Ground Plex, with no data leaving the AH data center boundary. Validation data is not persisted by the platform and is discarded at the end of the validation session. For security-sensitive environments such as Airbus Helicopters', validation should be performed against representative sample or synthetic data rather than live production data, consistent with standard integration development practice.

subsections.title: Error Handling & Pipeline Resilience
subsections.content:
Production-grade error handling is configurable at the individual Snap level and at the pipeline level. It is not bolt-on but built into the execution model.

- Per-Snap error pipelines: Each Snap can be configured to route error documents to a dedicated error-handling child pipeline rather than failing the entire pipeline. The error pipeline receives the failed record, the error message, and contextual metadata for logging, alerting, or reprocessing.
- Retry with backoff: Configurable retry policies on individual Snaps, covering maximum retry count, retry interval, and exponential backoff. Applied to transient failures (network timeouts, database connection drops) without human intervention.
- Dead-letter queue: Failed records that cannot be processed after all retries are routed to a dead-letter target (database table, file, message queue) for manual review and reprocessing. Full record context and error details are preserved.
- User-friendly error messages: Platform errors (SnapLogic infrastructure issues) and external system errors (database connection failures, API timeouts, schema mismatches) are surfaced with human-readable messages in the monitoring console and error logs, accessible to both developers and operations teams.

subsections.title: SnapGPT: Generative AI for Integration
subsections.content:
SnapGPT is SnapLogic's embedded generative AI assistant, accessible directly within the Designer. It operates from the SnapLogic Manager and processes only pipeline metadata and natural language prompts typed by developers. Airbus Helicopters' operational data is never accessed, processed, or transmitted by SnapGPT.

- Text2Pipeline: Describe an integration in plain English ("read all active items from Oracle inventory, filter out obsolete records, transform to the canonical product format, and load into PostgreSQL staging table") and SnapGPT generates a working pipeline with appropriate Snaps, connections, and basic configuration. Integration teams accelerate first-draft delivery by 60–80%. The generated pipeline runs within the Ground Plex and AH's data is never sent to SnapGPT.
- Auto-documentation: SnapGPT automatically generates human-readable descriptions for every pipeline, Snap, and field mapping in the Designer. Eliminates the documentation backlog that accumulates in every integration programme. Documentation is generated from pipeline metadata, with no data inspection required.
- AI-assisted debugging: When a pipeline fails, SnapGPT analyses the error context (error message, Snap configuration, schema details) and proposes a specific fix. Reduces mean time to resolution for production incidents without requiring senior developer involvement for every failure.
- Schema suggestion & Mapper generation: SnapGPT suggests field mappings between source and target schemas based on field names, data types, and semantic similarity. For complex transformations, SnapGPT generates the complete Mapper expression from a plain-language description of the desired output.
- Citizen Developer enablement: Business analysts and domain experts describe integration requirements in natural language. SnapGPT generates the pipeline. IT reviews and approves before production deployment, enabling a governed self-service model without sacrificing control.
- Describe Pipelines: SnapGPT can analyse an existing pipeline and produce a structured description of what it does, which systems it connects, what transformations are applied, and what the expected output is. Used for documentation, handover, and onboarding of new team members.

Figure~\ref{fig:snapgpt-describe} shows the SnapGPT: Describe the pipeline output, a structured analysis of a live pipeline.

[IMAGE:assets/images/airbus_rfp/snapgpt-describe-pipeline.png:SnapGPT: Describe the Pipeline:1.0:snapgpt-describe]



SnapGPT Pipeline Generation Interface Three aspects of SnapGPT's architecture are relevant in the context of an on-premises deployment. First, SnapGPT's AI features are fully available in a Ground Plex deployment , and they do not require air-gap-free network access or a SaaS execution environment to function. Second, SnapGPT processes only pipeline metadata (Snap types and connection topology) and the natural language prompts typed by developers. It never processes, transmits, or retains Airbus Helicopters' operational data, schema definitions, or field-level business logic . Third, SnapGPT is included in SnapLogic's standard enterprise subscription and is not a separately licensed AI premium tier.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: For the Airbus Helicopters integration team, the development model will be immediately productive. Existing Informatica developers recognise the source-transform-target pipeline paradigm from day one. SnapGPT accelerates first-draft pipeline delivery for both experienced developers and new team members. The citizen developer programme enables business analysts in engineering and procurement to build governed integrations without central IT dependency. The full GitLab CI/CD integration fits directly into AH's existing DevOps toolchain, and the four-environment lifecycle (Development, Validation, Pre-Production, Production) maps to AH's standard software delivery governance, with the Pre-Production environment providing a production-equivalent validation gate before any change reaches live workloads.

subsections.title: Governance, Security, Version Control & Lifecycle Management
subsections.content: This section addresses the governance and security requirements of the RFP: role-based access control with Active Directory integration (G-01, G-02), multi-factor authentication (G-03), SSO (G-04), service account and API key management (G-05, G-06), GitLab v18 integration for pipeline lifecycle (G-07, G-08), data lineage and impact analysis (G-09, G-10), pipeline versioning (G-11), TLS encryption and encryption at rest (S-01, S-02), credential vault and enhanced encryption (S-03), least privilege runtime security (S-04), immutable audit trail with SIEM export (S-05), environment segregation (S-06), and the no-inbound-firewall hybrid architecture (S-07). SnapLogic's governance model covers enterprise-grade access control, audit capabilities, and development lifecycle management as standard. For an integration platform operating within Airbus Helicopters' security-governed, aerospace-regulated environment, each of these is a baseline requirement rather than an optional enhancement.

subsections.title: Identity, Authentication & Access Control
subsections.content:
- RBAC with AD group mapping: Granular Read / Write / Execute / Owner permissions applied at Org, Project Space, Project, and individual pipeline/account/file asset level via Access Control Lists. Active Directory groups map directly to SnapLogic RBAC roles, so user access is governed by AH's existing AD group membership with no duplicate provisioning required.
- SSO and Active Directory integration: SAML 2.0 SSO with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Okta, PingIdentity, and OpenAM. SnapLogic acts as a SAML Service Provider; users authenticate against AH's existing IdP. SSO applies to all account types: platform users, admin users, and Citizen Developer accounts.
- Multi-Factor Authentication: MFA is enforced for privileged accounts via Auth0 TOTP. For non-privileged remote access, MFA is configurable per user or organisation-wide. When SSO is active, MFA enforcement is delegated to AH's IdP, so existing corporate MFA policies apply automatically.
- Machine-to-machine authentication: Pipeline-to-system connections authenticate via service account credentials, API keys, OAuth 2.0 client credentials, or certificate-based mutual TLS. All credentials are stored encrypted in the Ground Plex credential vault and never transmitted to the SnapLogic Manager.
- Application resource access control: Fine-grained ACL model controls access to pipeline assets, credentials/accounts, and file resources post-authentication. Users can only execute pipelines and access accounts they have been explicitly granted permissions for.

subsections.title: Credential Protection & Encryption
subsections.content:
- Credential vault: Connector credentials (database usernames/passwords, API keys, certificates) are encrypted at rest using org-level asymmetric RSA key pairs (AES-256 server-side encryption in S3-backed storage). Credentials are decrypted only within the Ground Plex at execution time. The SnapLogic Manager never holds plaintext credentials.
- Enhanced Account Encryption - Bring Your Own Key (optional): An optional double-encryption mode where Airbus Helicopters retains the private RSA key used to encrypt all connector credentials. The SnapLogic control plane cannot decrypt credentials under any circumstances, including during support or maintenance activities. Only the Ground Plex, operating within AH's infrastructure and holding AH's private key, can decrypt them. This Bring Your Own Key capability ensures that credential sovereignty remains entirely with AH, providing the highest available level of separation between SnapLogic's cloud infrastructure and AH's system access credentials.
- Secrets manager integration: AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault are supported as external secrets stores. Pipeline credentials are retrieved from the secrets manager at execution time rather than stored in SnapLogic, enabling AH to manage all secrets lifecycle centrally.
- TLS 1.2+ encryption in transit: All platform communications enforce TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 supported). Cipher suites: AES-128/256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, ECDHE key exchange with forward secrecy. All platform requests are HTTPS-only. No unencrypted transport.
- Principle of least privilege: Ground Plex runtime agents operate with minimal required OS permissions. Pipeline execution on customer-deployed Groundplexes does not permit arbitrary filesystem access or external process creation outside the configured execution context.

subsections.title: Audit Trail & Compliance
subsections.content:
Figure~\ref{fig:monitor-activity-logs} shows the SnapLogic Monitor: Activity Logs audit trail, the tamper-evident record that records every pipeline execution.

[IMAGE:assets/images/airbus_rfp/snaplogic-activity-logs-audit.png:SnapLogic Monitor: Activity Logs Audit Trail:1.0:monitor-activity-logs]



Activity Logs and Audit Trail

- Immutable audit trail: Tamper-evident log of all user actions (login/logout, pipeline execution, configuration changes, ACL modifications, user provisioning), system events, and administrative operations. Each log entry carries timestamp, user identity, action type, affected asset, and result.
- Audit log export for SIEM: Activity logs are exportable as CSV on demand and can be scheduled for automated export to AH's SIEM (Splunk, Elasticsearch, QRadar). The native retention period is 90 days. Twelve-month retention is achieved by scheduling regular exports to AH's long-term log storage, which is a documented configuration pattern rather than a workaround.
- Data lineage: End-to-end lineage from source system through all transformation steps to the target system, visualised in the Manager UI as an interactive graph. Lineage metadata is exportable via the SnapLogic Metadata API for integration with AH's enterprise data catalogue.
- Impact analysis: The SnapLogic Dependency Viewer identifies all pipelines, child pipelines, and assets that reference a given source schema, account, or shared pipeline. When AH's source systems undergo schema changes (Oracle column additions, SAP IDOC format updates), impact analysis immediately shows which downstream pipelines are affected, enabling controlled, proactive change management.

subsections.title: Version Control, CI/CD & Environment Lifecycle
subsections.content:
- Native pipeline versioning: Every pipeline change creates an immutable version. Developers can compare versions, restore to any previous version, and view the complete change history, equivalent to Git commit history for pipeline artefacts.
- GitLab v18 integration: SnapLogic's native Git integration supports GitLab v18 (backward-compatible REST API and webhook schemas, confirmed). Pipeline artefacts (.slpkg packages) are committed to GitLab repositories via the SnapLogic Migration API. GitLab CI/CD pipelines trigger automatic deployment of promoted pipeline packages across all four Ground Plex environments: Development → Validation → Pre-Production → Production, with a designated approver gate at each promotion boundary.
- Multi-stage development lifecycle: Separate Ground Plex instances for Development, Validation, Pre-Production, and Production. Airbus Helicopters has confirmed the requirement for a dedicated Pre-Production environment to validate integrations against production-equivalent workloads and data volumes before promotion. Each environment has independent credentials, schedules, and RBAC controls. Pipeline promotion is controlled at each stage. RBAC prevents direct production deployment without an approved promotion workflow.
- Pre-Production environment: The Pre-Production Ground Plex is sized to match Production resource allocations, enabling validation of performance characteristics, connection pool behaviour, and concurrent pipeline throughput under realistic load. This environment is the final gate before production deployment and is used for integration testing, load validation, and sign-off. It is isolated from both the Validation environment and Production, with its own credentials and RBAC assignments. CI/CD-triggered promotions from Validation to Pre-Production require a designated approver role in GitLab before the deployment pipeline proceeds.
- Physical/logical environment segregation: Development, Validation, Pre-Production, and Production Ground Plex instances are isolated at the infrastructure level. No shared credentials or accounts exist across environments. Separate OpenShift namespaces are recommended for full network-level isolation between all four environments.
- Programmatic platform configuration: Full REST API for Org management, user and group provisioning, ACL configuration, and Ground Plex management, enabling Infrastructure-as-Code patterns for the SnapLogic environment itself (Ansible, Terraform, GitLab CI).

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: The governance model maps directly to AH's existing Active Directory structure, SSO provider, and OpenShift RBAC, requiring no parallel identity infrastructure. The no-inbound-firewall architecture satisfies AH's network security posture without requiring firewall rule exceptions on the perimeter. The Enhanced Account Encryption option gives AH full control over credential decryption keys, ensuring that SnapLogic infrastructure cannot access AH's system credentials under any circumstances, including during support or maintenance activities.

subsections.title: Observability, Monitoring & Error Management
subsections.content: This section covers the observability and monitoring requirements of the RFP: the centralised monitoring console (O-01), Ground Plex node resource monitoring (O-02), administrative operations console (O-02.4.1), Dynatrace OTel integration (O-03), Elasticsearch export (O-04), Splunk integration (O-05), REST API metrics and log access (O-06), event-based notifications (O-07), and audit trail retention of three months or more (O-08). SnapLogic provides a unified monitoring console covering pipeline execution status, Ground Plex node resource utilisation, scheduling, and operational alerts. All monitoring data is generated within and accessible from Airbus Helicopters' own infrastructure, and the observability stack integrates with AH's existing monitoring tooling without requiring a separate platform.

subsections.title: Centralised Monitoring Console
subsections.content:

subsections.title: Log & Metrics Export to AH's Observability Stack

- Dynatrace: Native OpenTelemetry (OTel) support. Ground Plex emits OTel-compatible trace and metric data that feeds directly into Dynatrace OneAgent and OTel ingest endpoints. Pipeline execution traces appear in Dynatrace distributed tracing without custom instrumentation.

- Splunk Enterprise: Native Splunk Snap Pack for log and metrics streaming to on-premises Splunk Enterprise instances. Pipeline execution events, error events, and audit log entries are delivered in Splunk CIM-compatible format.
- Prometheus / Grafana: JMX metrics endpoint exposed by Ground Plex nodes, scrapeable by Prometheus. Pre-built Grafana dashboard templates available for pipeline throughput, error rates, and node resource visualisation.

subsections.content:

- Event-based notifications: Webhook callbacks configurable for pipeline completion, failure, SLA breach, and node health events. Notification targets include email, Slack, PagerDuty, SNMP traps, and any webhook-capable system. Enables event-driven operational workflows (auto-escalation, auto-remediation triggers).
- Comprehensive audit trail: Minimum 3-month native retention of all pipeline execution and user activity logs. Extended retention via scheduled export to AH's SIEM or log archive.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters

subsections.title: Data Quality, Validation & Trust
subsections.content: This section covers the data trust and quality requirements of the RFP: inline data validation and automated assessment (DT-01, DT-02), PII and sensitive data protection (DT-03), identity resolution and deduplication (DT-04), exception management and reprocessing workflows (DT-05), reusable validation policies (DT-06), and DQ trend monitoring via AH's existing BI tooling (DT-07). SnapLogic implements data quality enforcement inline within the pipeline execution flow. Airbus Helicopters can build validation, profiling, and exception management directly into the integration architecture, without a separate dedicated DQ tooling layer.

subsections.title: Inline Validation & Data Assessment
subsections.content:
- Inline data validation: The Validate Snap and Filter Snap enforce data quality constraints within the pipeline, including null checks, range validation, referential integrity, format validation, and custom expression-based rules. Invalid records are rejected, flagged with an error code, routed to an error pipeline, or quarantined to a DQ hold table based on configurable policy.
- Automated data assessment: Schema inference during pipeline development automatically profiles source data, covering null patterns, data type distributions, row counts, distinct value counts, min/max values, and frequency histograms. This provides integration developers with a quality baseline before production deployment and surfaces data quality issues early in the development lifecycle.
- Centralised, reusable validation policies: Validation logic is encapsulated in shared child pipelines, promoted through the standard Development → Validation → Pre-Production → Production lifecycle and reused across multiple integration projects. Changes to validation rules are deployed once and propagate to all consuming pipelines via the shared child pipeline reference.

subsections.title: PII & Sensitive Data Protection
subsections.content:
- Data masking: The Mask Snap applies configurable masking strategies (full mask, partial mask, format-preserving tokenisation) to sensitive fields inline in the pipeline. Masked data never reaches non-authorised downstream systems.
- Hashing & obfuscation: Expression-based SHA-256/MD5 hashing, pseudonymisation, and obfuscation are available for any pipeline field. Applied at the Mapper Snap level, with no additional tooling required.
- PII field identification: Sensitive field identification uses pattern matching (regular expressions for formats like national IDs, email addresses, IBAN, credit card numbers) applied via the Filter or Validate Snap. Identified PII fields trigger downstream masking or routing rules.

subsections.title: Identity Resolution & Deduplication
subsections.content:
SnapLogic supports record deduplication and identity resolution patterns natively through standard Snap combinations, which is directly relevant to AH's master data management and supplier data consolidation use cases.

- Exact deduplication: Sort Snap + Group By Snap + Aggregate Snap combination for deterministic deduplication on exact key matches (part number, supplier ID, DUNS number).
- Fuzzy matching: Script Snap with Python (using libraries such as fuzzywuzzy , rapidfuzz , or recordlinkage ) enables probabilistic entity matching for cases where exact key deduplication is insufficient (e.g., supplier name variations, address normalisation).
- Unified view construction: Lookup Snap and Join Snap patterns merge records from multiple source systems into a unified canonical view, supporting master data hub patterns within the integration pipeline.

subsections.title: Exception Management & Quality Workflow
subsections.content:
- Failed record routing: Records failing validation rules are routed to configurable error targets (database table, file, message queue) with the full original record, the failed rule, the error message, and a timestamp. No valid data is lost; no processing stops.
- Authorisation-based reprocessing: SnapLogic's Triggered Task API enables AH to build approval and reprocessing workflows: a data steward reviews quarantined records via an external application, approves corrections, and triggers a reprocessing pipeline via API. SnapLogic provides the execution substrate. The approval UI is built by AH or SnapLogic PS.
- DQ trend monitoring: Pipeline execution statistics (error rates, record counts, rejection rates per pipeline) are tracked over time in the monitoring console and exportable via the REST API. Export to Elasticsearch or Splunk enables custom DQ dashboards within AH's existing BI infrastructure. Note: SnapLogic does not include a dedicated DQ visualisation module. AH's existing observability tooling (Grafana, Kibana, Splunk) serves as the visualisation layer.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: Airbus Helicopters operates in a regulated aerospace manufacturing environment where data quality directly affects supply chain integrity, component traceability, and regulatory compliance. Several characteristics of AH's integration landscape make inline data quality enforcement critical: the heterogeneous source landscape (Oracle, MSSQL, PostgreSQL, S2000M, STEP) produces data with inconsistent formats, encoding, and completeness across systems; supplier master data consolidation across multiple procurement systems requires identity resolution and deduplication; and GDPR obligations require consistent PII masking for any integration touching personnel, supplier contact, or partner data. SnapLogic's inline validation model means quality rules are enforced at the integration layer itself, not as a separate downstream process. For AH's migration from Informatica, existing data quality logic embedded in mappings is carried forward via SLIM's automated conversion, reducing the risk of quality regressions during the migration programme. Exception records and reprocessing workflows can be integrated directly into AH's existing operational tooling via the REST API, without a separate DQ platform licence or infrastructure.

subsections.title: Migration from Existing Integration Tools
subsections.content: This section addresses the migration requirements of the RFP: automated Informatica PowerCenter and IICS migration via the SLIM tooling (M-01), migration from other ETL tools including Talend, SSIS, and DataStage (M-02), and the post-migration validation framework (M-03). The RFP's explicit requirement for Informatica PowerCenter / IICS migration capability reflects a real and significant concern: Airbus Helicopters has invested years of engineering effort in existing Informatica pipelines. SnapLogic's migration tooling is designed to preserve that investment rather than force a complete re-development from scratch. Evaluators should directly ask any competing vendor whether they provide automated migration tooling for Informatica PowerCenter pipelines, and if so, request a live demonstration of that tooling against a representative sample of AH's existing mappings. A vendor that proposes a migration primarily based on manual re-implementation or professional services effort, without an automated conversion layer, is proposing that Airbus Helicopters fund the rebuild of its own pipeline estate. That is a significantly different cost and risk profile than what SnapLogic's SLIM tooling delivers.

subsections.title: SLIM - SnapLogic Intelligent Modernizer
subsections.content:
SLIM (SnapLogic Intelligent Modernizer) is an agentic AI-powered migration tool that automates the conversion of existing ETL pipelines from legacy tools to SnapLogic. The name reflects the philosophy: a leaner, faster migration path that does not require AH to carry the full weight of a ground-up rebuild.

Figure~\ref{fig:slim-arch} illustrates the four-phase SLIM workflow.

[IMAGE:assets/images/airbus_rfp/snaplogic-slim-architecture.png:SnapLogic Intelligent Modernizer - SLIM:1.0:slim-arch]



SLIM Migration Architecture: Automated Informatica Migration

- Analysis phase: SLIM connects to the source Informatica repository and analyses all mappings, workflows, and reusable components. It produces a migration complexity assessment, categorising pipelines as straightforward (automated conversion), moderate (automated with review), or complex (manual SE involvement required).
- Automated conversion: SLIM generates equivalent SnapLogic pipelines from Informatica mappings. Source-to-target field mappings, transformation logic, lookup patterns, and error handling constructs are converted automatically. Conversion coverage and fidelity depend on the Informatica version and feature set in use. SnapLogic PS will confirm exact coverage for AH's Informatica environment during the initial assessment.
- Supported sources: Informatica PowerCenter and IICS are the primary supported sources. SLIM also supports migration from Talend, SSIS (SQL Server Integration Services), IBM DataStage, and Ab Initio, with coverage varying by tool and version.
- Iterative refinement: The agentic SLIM engine supports iterative refinement cycles, reviewing generated pipelines, identifying conversion gaps, and regenerating with additional context. Complex business logic that cannot be auto-converted is flagged for SE review rather than silently approximated.
- Migration effort reduction: Organisations using SLIM consistently report 40–70% reduction in overall migration effort compared to manual re-development, with the highest savings on high-volume, structurally consistent mapping libraries. For a migration of typical enterprise scale, the difference between an automated conversion tooling approach and a manual re-implementation approach is measured in months of PS effort and the associated cost and project risk, not incremental optimisation.

subsections.title: Migration Validation & Testing Framework
subsections.content:
Automated conversion alone is not sufficient for a production migration. SnapLogic PS provides a structured validation methodology as part of the migration engagement.

- Record-by-record output comparison: Post-conversion pipelines are executed against a representative data set and their outputs compared record-by-record to the source Informatica pipeline outputs. Discrepancies are logged for investigation and correction.
- Regression testing: A regression test suite is built during migration that can be re-executed against future SnapLogic platform updates to ensure ongoing fidelity.
- Performance validation: Converted pipelines are benchmarked against the original Informatica execution times for equivalent data volumes. Performance tuning (Ultra Pipelines, node sizing, parallelism configuration) is applied where necessary.

A dimension of the migration decision that extends beyond the immediate programme is long-term platform flexibility . SnapLogic pipelines are stored as human-readable JSON with a fully documented schema, a deliberate architectural choice that preserves Airbus Helicopters' ability to inspect, export, and if necessary migrate pipeline logic in the future. The existence of SLIM itself reflects this philosophy: a vendor that invests in automated tooling to migrate customers onto its platform from others is demonstrably less reliant on lock-in as a retention mechanism than one that does not. Airbus Helicopters' pipeline investment on SnapLogic is portable, documented, and not dependent on proprietary binary formats or opaque transformation languages.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: For Airbus Helicopters, SLIM represents a concrete answer to one of the most significant risks in this programme: the cost and timeline of migrating the existing Informatica pipeline estate. Rather than treating migration as a separate, open-ended professional services engagement, SLIM gives the evaluation committee a quantifiable starting point for migration scope, effort, and timeline before contract signature. The assessment phase can be initiated during the evaluation period, giving AH a factual basis for comparing migration approaches across competing vendors.

subsections.title: Scalability, High Availability & Disaster Recovery
subsections.content: This section covers the scalability, high availability, and disaster recovery requirements of the RFP: distributed processing and horizontal scaling (P-02), active-active high availability with automatic failover (P-03), and disaster recovery across data center sites or OpenShift availability zones (P-05). SnapLogic's Ground Plex architecture is stateless by design: pipeline definitions, schedules, and configuration are stored in the Manager, not on the node itself. This makes scaling, high availability, and disaster recovery operational procedures rather than engineering projects. Adding capacity or recovering from a node failure does not require pipeline re-architecture or redeployment.

subsections.title: Distributed Processing & Scaling
subsections.content:
- Horizontal node scaling: Additional Ground Plex worker nodes are added to the existing Snaplex group and immediately begin receiving pipeline workloads. No pipeline re-architecture, re-deployment, or downtime. OpenShift Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) policies apply directly to Ground Plex pods, and workload-driven autoscaling is natively supported.
- Vertical scaling: CPU and memory resources per Ground Plex pod are configurable via Helm values. Increasing node resources raises the concurrency capacity (simultaneous pipeline executions per node).
- Ultra Pipeline throughput: Ultra Pipelines (SnapLogic's high-performance streaming execution mode) sustain billions of records per day on appropriately sized Ground Plex deployments. SnapLogic PS provides sizing guidance based on AH's expected data volumes, peak throughput requirements, and pipeline complexity profile.
- Pipeline concurrency: Multiple JCC containers per Ground Plex node can be configured to increase the number of simultaneously running pipelines. Concurrency is configurable per Snaplex and per node.

subsections.title: High Availability
subsections.content:
- Active-active multi-node HA: All Ground Plex nodes in a Snaplex are active simultaneously. Incoming pipeline execution requests are distributed across available nodes. Node failure is detected within the 20-second heartbeat interval; failed nodes are removed from the active pool and pending work is redistributed to healthy nodes with no pipeline interruption for stateless workloads.
- No single point of failure: The Ground Plex execution layer has no single point of failure when deployed with 2+ nodes. The SnapLogic Manager (cloud) is operated by SnapLogic with 99.95% uptime SLA. Manager availability does not affect the execution of already-deployed and scheduled pipelines.
- Scheduled pipeline resilience: Scheduled pipelines that are interrupted by a node failure are automatically restarted on available nodes within the same Snaplex.

subsections.title: Disaster Recovery
subsections.content:
- Ground Plex DR deployment: Ground Plex nodes can be deployed across AH's primary and secondary data center sites (or across OpenShift availability zones). DR Ground Plex nodes register to the same SnapLogic Org and are immediately active, able to receive workloads if the primary site is unavailable.
- Manager metadata backup & restore: SnapLogic Manager metadata (pipeline definitions, accounts, schedules, user configurations) is backed up by SnapLogic with a 30-day retention. In a full Manager restoration scenario, RPO is 2 hours and RTO is 48 hours. Customers can also export pipeline packages (.slpkg) to their own Git repository for independent backup.
- Stateless Ground Plex recovery: Ground Plex nodes are fully stateless and hold no persistent data. A new Ground Plex node, pointed at the same SnapLogic Org, is operational within minutes of deployment. Recovery of the execution layer is independent of the Manager recovery timeline.

subsections.title: Relevance for Airbus Helicopters
subsections.content: Airbus Helicopters' integration platform must support continuous manufacturing and supply chain operations across a multi-site environment, making scalability and availability non-negotiable. The Ground Plex architecture maps directly to AH's OpenShift infrastructure: additional nodes are registered to the same Snaplex and immediately accept workloads, providing elastic horizontal scale without pipeline modifications or downtime. The active-active HA model, with automatic failover on 20-second heartbeat detection, eliminates any single point of failure in the execution layer. For AH's four-environment deployment (Development, Validation, Pre-Production, Production), each Ground Plex Snaplex is independently sized: Development and Validation environments run at reduced resource allocation; the Pre-Production environment is sized to match Production to enable realistic load and throughput validation before promotion. The stateless Ground Plex recovery model is particularly advantageous in OpenShift: pod restarts, node evictions, and cluster maintenance events do not result in data loss or pipeline corruption, since no operational state is held on the pod. AH's OpenShift team can apply standard Kubernetes operational practices (rolling updates, resource quota adjustments, node maintenance drains) without special coordination with the SnapLogic integration team.

subsections.title: IT/OT Integration Architecture
subsections.content:
Airbus Helicopters operates a multi-layered integration landscape that includes traditional IT systems (ERP, data warehouses, business applications) and operational technology (OT) platforms (PLM, MES, SCADA, shop-floor data collectors). Integration between IT and OT has historically been constrained by the need for protocol-specific gateways, limited batch windows, and the operational risk of directly connecting business intelligence tools to production control systems. SnapLogic addresses this with native support for OPC UA (the industrial IoT standard), Kafka-based streaming integration, and containerised Ground Plex deployment that can be co-located with OT infrastructure without exposing it to the corporate network.

For Airbus Helicopters, three specific integration patterns become feasible with SnapLogic that are difficult or operationally risky with API-management-only tooling:

1. **PLM-to-ERP Bill of Materials (BOM) synchronisation:** Engineering change orders approved in the PLM system trigger real-time updates to SAP or Oracle ERP, with full audit trail, conflict detection, and rollback capability. SnapLogic's Triggered Task execution mode supports this pattern without batch latency.
2. **MES production data aggregation for BI:** Real-time or near-real-time integration of production metrics (cycle time, quality measurements, equipment utilisation) from shop-floor MES systems into enterprise BI platforms, with data cleansing, anomaly detection, and enrichment performed inline by the Ground Plex before delivery to the data warehouse.
3. **Supply chain event streaming:** Change Data Capture from supplier-facing systems (procurement, logistics, quality) streamed via Kafka to downstream analytics and operational dashboards, enabling real-time visibility into supply chain disruption and bottleneck formation.

SnapLogic's Ground Plex can be deployed in a DMZ or edge configuration, physically or logically separated from the main IT network, with data moved across network boundaries only after validation and sanitisation. This satisfies both the IT security requirement (no direct OT-to-corporate-network connectivity) and the OT reliability requirement (integration workload does not impose load on production control systems). The architecture is directly comparable to patterns deployed at Schneider Electric (OT integration at scale) and Boehringer Ingelheim (GxP-regulated OT data flows).

For the Airbus Helicopters evaluation, IT/OT integration should be treated as a Phase 2 capability, validated during the pilot programme but not a hard requirement for initial deployment. The capability is included in the platform subscription at no additional cost.

subsections.title: Citizen Developer Programme
subsections.content:
One of the stated objectives in the RFP is enabling business analysts and domain experts to build integrations without depending on the central IT integration team for every new data flow. SnapLogic supports this through SnapGPT-enabled Text2Pipeline generation, governed Snap Pack libraries, and IT-controlled approval workflows. The citizen developer model is not ungoverned self-service; it is governed, audited, delegated authority within boundaries set by IT.

The governance model works as follows:

- **IT defines permitted Snaps and connections:** The SnapLogic administrator configures which Snap Packs are available to which user groups. A citizen developer in procurement might have access to CSV, Excel, REST API, and PostgreSQL Snaps, but not Oracle, Snowflake, or SAP connectors. Connections to production systems are pre-configured and credential-protected by IT, so the citizen developer never handles database passwords or API keys directly.
- **Pipelines are subject to the same RBAC and audit trail as IT-developed integrations:** Every pipeline execution, regardless of who built it, is logged, monitored, and subject to the same error handling and alerting framework. There is no separate "citizen integration runtime" with weaker governance.
- **IT approval workflow for production promotion:** A pipeline built in the Development environment by a citizen developer cannot be promoted to Production without IT approval. The approval process is configurable: it can be as simple as a Slack notification with a one-click approval link, or as structured as a ServiceNow change request integrated into AH's existing ITSM workflow.
- **SnapGPT is optional and can be disabled:** If Airbus Helicopters determines that AI-assisted pipeline generation introduces unacceptable risk or complexity, SnapGPT can be disabled at the organisation level, and the citizen developer programme can proceed using template-based pipelines and drag-and-drop construction only.

The business case for a citizen developer programme is reduced backlog in the central integration team and faster time-to-value for departmental data flows that do not require enterprise-scale orchestration. The risk case is ungoverned proliferation of fragile, undocumented integrations. SnapLogic's model addresses the risk case through IT-enforced boundaries and full auditability, while delivering the business case through genuine ease of use. Siemens / Siemens Healthineers operates a comparable model at enterprise scale, with over 200 citizen developers building governed integrations across manufacturing and supply chain functions.

For the Airbus Helicopters evaluation, the citizen developer programme should be validated during the pilot with 2-3 representative users from engineering and procurement. The capability is included in the platform subscription at no additional cost, and SnapGPT training is included in the Platinum Support package (50 seats).

subsections.title: Agent Integration via MCP
subsections.content:
SnapLogic has implemented support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an emerging open standard for AI agent integration. MCP allows AI agents (such as Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT models, or enterprise-deployed LLMs) to query data sources, trigger workflows, and retrieve context in real time through a standardised protocol. SnapLogic pipelines can be exposed as MCP servers, allowing AI agents to invoke them as tools during reasoning and task execution.

Figure~\ref{fig:mcp-server} illustrates the SnapLogic MCP server architecture and integration with AI agents.

[IMAGE:assets/images/airbus_rfp/snaplogic-mcp-server.png:SnapLogic as MCP Server:1.0:mcp-server]

For Airbus Helicopters, this enables two specific use cases:

1. **Conversational data access for engineering teams:** An engineer asks an AI assistant, "What is the current inventory level for part number AH-7734-B across all European warehouses?" The AI agent uses MCP to invoke a SnapLogic pipeline that queries the ERP system, aggregates results, and returns the answer in natural language. The pipeline enforces the same RBAC, audit trail, and data masking rules as any other integration, so the AI agent operates within AH's governance framework, not as a privileged bypass.
2. **AI-driven workflow orchestration:** An AI agent is tasked with processing a supplier quality alert. The agent uses MCP to invoke SnapLogic pipelines that retrieve the affected part records from PLM, check current production schedules in MES, notify the procurement team via email, and log the incident in the quality management system. The entire workflow is auditable, and the AI agent's actions are subject to the same approval and exception handling rules as human-triggered workflows.

SnapLogic's MCP implementation runs within the Ground Plex, so all data access and transformation occurs on-premises. The AI agent communicates with the SnapLogic MCP server via the same outbound-only HTTPS connection that the Designer and Manager use. No additional firewall rules or network exposure is required.

MCP support is a forward-looking capability, and Airbus Helicopters should not treat it as a hard requirement for the initial deployment. However, it is a differentiator in the evaluation: no other on-premises ETL/ELT platform included in this RFP offers comparable AI agent integration capability. The capability is included in the platform subscription at no additional cost.
